title: US government map of Africa mislabels every country at global conference
description:
State department ‘takes full responsibility’ for erroneous, widely shared chart displayed at Aids conference in Brazil

A US government map of Africa mislabeled every country during a state department presentation at a ⁠global conference in Brazil ⁠this week, ​causing a stir among attenders who took screenshots and posted them online.

Reuters viewed a video of the presentation given at the Aids 2026 conference in ⁠Rio de Janeiro, which shows the errant map displayed halfway during a presentation about the state department’s new health agreements.

Continue reading...
summary: A US government map of Africa was mislabeled during a presentation at the Aids 2026 conference in Brazil, causing a stir among attendees. The State Department took full responsibility for the error. The map was displayed during a presentation about new health agreements.

title: Fifteen elephant deaths at Kenya park may be due to cyanide poisoning
description:
Analysis of samples collected from carcasses found traces of toxic chemical compound, says Kenya Wildlife Service

The recent deaths of 15 elephants near a park in southern Kenya in the past month were most likely caused by the animals ingesting pesticides used on nearby tomato farms, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) has said.

Erustus Kanga, the agency’s director general, told Citizen TV that analysis of samples collected from the carcasses had found traces of cyanide, a chemical compound used in farming as a predator control poison and a pest fumigant, which has also been used by poachers.

Continue reading...
summary: The Kenya Wildlife Service has found that 15 elephant deaths near a park in southern Kenya were likely caused by cyanide poisoning from pesticides used on nearby tomato farms. Analysis of samples from the carcasses revealed the presence of cyanide, a chemical compound used in farming and by poachers. This incident highlights the impact of human activities on wildlife.

title: Fifty-three days and counting: 93-year-old leader’s record absence fuels health speculation
description:
Cameroon’s Paul Biya has not made a statement or been seen since leaving for ‘brief private stay’ at Swiss hotel on 7 June

A record 53-day absence by the world’s oldest head of state has renewed speculation in his native Cameroon about whether he is dead or alive, even though discussing his health is illegal in the country.

On 7 June, 93-year-old Paul Biya left for Switzerland for what officials described as a “brief private stay” alongside his wife, Chantal. Almost two months later, neither the president nor the first lady have addressed the country or been seen publicly.

Continue reading...
summary: Cameroon's 93-year-old President Paul Biya has been absent for 53 days, sparking speculation about his health, despite a ban on discussing his condition in the country. He left for a "brief private stay" in Switzerland on June 7 with his wife, but neither of them has been seen or addressed the public since then. The prolonged absence has raised concerns about his well-being.

title: A quarter of young Africans believe USAID cuts could be positive, survey finds
description:
Losing funds should force leaders to confront their own challenges, they said, while many voiced concerns over increasing foreign influence

A quarter of young Africans believe aid cuts by the US could have a positive impact, saying that losing foreign money will force leaders to confront and solve their own challenges, according to a new survey.

In Ghana and Nigeria, almost half (41% and 40% respectively) of young people aged 18 to 24 were optimistic, with Liberia not far behind (37%). A further one in 10 (11%) young people were uncertain about the impact, according to the African Youth Survey, which interviewed almost 5,000 people across 16 of the continent’s 54 recognised countries.

Continue reading...
summary: A survey of young Africans found that a quarter of them believe US aid cuts could have a positive impact, as it may force leaders to address their own challenges. The survey, which interviewed over 5,000 people across 16 countries, showed varying levels of optimism in Ghana, Nigeria, and Liberia. Many respondents also expressed concerns about increasing foreign influence.

title: Kenya investigating unexpected deaths of 15 elephants in national park

The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said 10 of the elephants showed signs of partial paralysis before dying within two days.

summary: Kenya's Amboseli national park is investigating the deaths of 15 elephants, with 10 showing signs of partial paralysis before dying within two days, and a potential toxic substance detected in several of the elephants. The Kenya Wildlife Service is leading the investigation. The incident has raised concerns about the health and well-being of the elephants in the park.
